Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim

Class QuestNavSimDevice

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim.QuestNavSimDevice
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public class QuestNavSimDevice extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Registers the simulated headset as a HAL SimDevice, so it shows up on its own in the Sim GUI's "Other Devices" panel under the QuestNav node, just as the simulated Limelight shows up under Limelight.

Outside simulation SimDevice.create returns null and the whole class becomes a no-op.

The three switches

The kInput fields are the genuinely useful part: you tick them from the Sim GUI, on the fly, without recompiling or moving the robot.
  • Force Tracking Loss — the Quest loses features. On recovery, the pose comes back displaced.
  • Force Pose Jump — the double-tap to passthrough. The pose jumps but isTracking stays true, which is the treacherous part.
  • Force Link Loss — loose cable. Publishing stops and the robot sees isConnected() fall.

 var sim = new SimDeviceSim("QuestNav:questnav", 0);
 sim.getBoolean("Force Tracking Loss").set(true);
 double drift = sim.getDouble("Drift (m)").get();

    • clearPoseJumpRequest

      public void clearPoseJumpRequest()
      Clears the pose-jump switch. It is a pulse, not a state: if it stayed ticked, the pose would jump every cycle and the Sim GUI would have no way to send a single jump.
